report:
Reviewed the complete heading claim and its single ordinary implementation and single ordinary test association; no TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. In spec.rs, parse_anchors handles every Markdown Heading start without filtering level and closes at range.start through finish_anchor. That helper trims preceding whitespace, stores the preceding content, and takes the active anchor, so following prose remains excluded until a new valid definition establishes active state. Both ATX and Setext parser headings use this path; HTML examples are excluded by the HTML guard. The associated every_atx_and_setext_heading_closes_content_until_a_new_definition test visibly iterates all six ATX levels and both Setext forms, asserts no diagnostics, exact multi-paragraph preceding content, an end span before the heading, and exact fresh content after a new definition. Retaining the heading or intervening prose, dropping the qualification, or failing to restart would violate those assertions. Captured the source fixture helper, which only copies its filename and supplied text into SpecSource.

Baseline verification: current implementation is byte-identical to the historical reviewed implementation. The test-file delta only changes an unrelated review inventory assertion from claim to claim-fragment access; the associated heading test is unchanged. Independently checked the prior rationale against the current captured claim, metadata, implementation and complete associated test. Its reference to offsets is supported by the boundary inequality, not an exact numeric offset assertion; exact content and source inspection account for the boundary guarantee. No changes needed.

Execution: personally ran review start, review read, and source/baseline comparison commands; no behavioral tests or builds were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing sage-meta functional tests and successful root cargo build; that execution is not inferred from annotations or claimed as my own.
